evidence.positive: Against the running c45154016 build (demo-demo tenant): logged in as admin, minted a tenant API token (POST /api/admin/tokens/tenant/demo-demo -> 201), POSTed a BSM log entry with X-API-Key to /api/bsm/logs (BSMLog was @Audited pre-fix) -> 200 "Logs received successfully"; log showed `Successfully saved 1 BSM log entries for tenant: TenantKey[value=demo-demo]` and the row appeared in "demo-demo".bsm_logs (machine_name loop-or2964-positive). Created a patient via POST /api/admin/patients/ -> 200 (pmrn or2964positive-fake-...), an operation via /operations/create -> 200 (caseId 74528, row present in "demo-demo".operations), and read it back through OperationRepository (formerly a RevisionRepository) via GET /api/admin/patients/by-pmrn/{pmrn}/operations -> 200 with the same operationId. loopuser form login -> 200 and /api/user/info -> 200 (User was @Audited). Startup log: `Started OrciApplication` with no errors.
evidence.negative: Running JVM command line (/proc/1/cmdline) contains no envers jar (grep -c envers = 0; hibernate-core 7.4.5, spring-data-jpa 4.1.1 present). /actuator/beans (admin session) listed 91 *Repository beans and zero beans whose name or type matches envers|Revision; tenantRepository is defined by @EnableJpaRepositories on DatabaseConfiguration; /actuator/env has no property matching envers. After the writes above, information_schema in database orci showed 421 tables across public, demo-demo, mgb-mgh, mgb-icsnh, mayo-mayo with zero tables matching %_aud, %_audit or %revinfo% (only AuditService's audit_events exists). docker logs for the whole run before the red check: 0 lines matching envers|revinfo|_aud.
evidence.red_check: Flipped by re-injecting Envers into the disposable container: copied hibernate-envers-7.4.5.Final.jar (exact runtime Hibernate version) into /app/libs, appended it to /app/jib-classpath-file, and placed a pre-fix (parent-commit) BSMLog.class compiled with @Audited into /app/classes/com/guided/orci/models/logging so it shadowed the shipped class; docker restart; JVM cmdline then showed the envers jar and the app booted. Repeating the BSM POST returned 500 "Failed to save logs" and the log showed Envers' AuditProcess.doBeforeTransactionCompletion -> DefaultRevisionInfoGenerator.saveRevisionData failing with `ERROR: relation "revinfo_seq" does not exist` ([select nextval('revinfo_seq')]); no bsm_logs row was committed, while the non-@Audited patient/operation writes in the same run still succeeded. Reverted: restored jib-classpath-file (sha256 8d2fd524... matches backup), removed the jar and the injected class dir (ls /app/libs sha256 fb326f33... matches pre-injection; logging dir absent), docker restart, cmdline envers count 0, 0 envers/revinfo log lines since that start, BSM POST -> 200 with row loop-or2964-revert persisted, audit-table count still 0.

caveats: CRUD was exercised on a sample of the formerly audited entities (BSMLog, Patient, Operation, User, APIToken) rather than all 45; the rest are covered only by successful entity-mapping at boot.

The red check re-injected Envers for one entity (BSMLog) rather than running the full pre-fix build; the pre-fix DatabaseConfiguration was not swapped because spring-data-envers is gone from the runtime and it could only fail to load.
Spring-data-envers RevisionRepository removal was verified via actuator bean inspection and normal repository reads, not by invoking findRevisions (no caller exists, per the ticket).

automation.assessment: The removal is mechanical and nothing at runtime depends on it; the commit already deleted the only Envers-specific test (MedicationRepositoryTest revision lookup) and repository tests boot with plain @EnableJpaRepositories, so the existing backend suite exercises every entity mapping. The only regression worth guarding is the dependency creeping back in, which is a build-level check, not an app test.
proposed_tests: Maven enforcer bannedDependencies rule (root pom) for org.springframework.data:spring-data-envers and org.hibernate.orm:hibernate-envers so a transitive or copy-pasted reintroduction fails the build.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: On the main build, writes and reads to formerly audited entities (BSM log, patient, operation, user login) all succeeded and the rows landed in the tenant schema.
Negative: The running JVM has no Envers jar, the Spring context has no Envers or revision beans or properties, and no audit or revinfo tables exist in any schema after the writes.
Red check: Re-injecting the Envers jar plus a pre-fix @Audited BSMLog class made the same write fail with relation revinfo_seq does not exist; the container was restored by checksum and the write passed again.

Automation: Nothing app-level is worth adding; a Maven enforcer ban on spring-data-envers and hibernate-envers would stop the dependency from returning.
